rules_text:
Rules summary Dragon Castle concise reference by hecose Setup: • Board – 1 Spirit card, 1 Dragon card, fill countdown tokens according to #players, extras stacked on leftmost space. • Player – 1 shrine. Concepts: • Available tile = at least one long side not blocked. • Adjacent = orthogonally, not diagonally. Different levels OK. Turn: • 1 Mandatory Action: a) Take 1 tile from top floor, then exact matching tile from any floor. b) Take 1 tile from top floor and 1 shrine. c) Take 1 tile from top floor, then discard facedown for 1VP. d) Summon dragon. Allowed when only floor 1 tiles left. Claim rightmost countdown token (worth 2VP). Once exclamation mark revealed, play until end of round. • Put claimed tiles on own board, on free space or facedown tile, never on faceup tile or shrine. • If any 4+ adjacent tiles are of same colour, must consolidate by flipping facedown and scoring. • When consolidating, may build shrine from own pool onto newly consolidated tiles. Faction(red/green/yellow) tiles allow 1 shrine, Special tiles(blue/black) allow 2, Dragon tile(Purple) also gives 1VP. • 1 Optional Action: discard faceup tiles or shrine to activate Spirit power. Game end scoring: VP tokens collected Countdown tokens Dragon card objective Shrines score 1/2/3VP at floors 1/2/3+ Tiebreaker: most facedown stacks, then shrines Other notes: • For Spirit cards and Dragon cards, refer pages 12 – 15. # of tiles / VP 4 / 2 5 / 3 6 / 5 7 / 6 8 / 8 > 8 / +1

Whoever accepted the production standards of this game had possibly never seen or felt a real Mahjong tile - the cheap plastic here was a million miles away from that. [Rating: 3/10] Played the game in Essen, my friend was about to buy the game when a table opened up, so we decided to play a quick round first, great decision because none of us liked the game, yes the stones are lovely, but the player papers and set up paper were very disappointing, gameplay didn't capture us at all, we actually stopped playing the game before we were done because we just couldn't care anymore.

[Rating: 3/10] They were tempting fate with the company name.  Nothing bad but absolutely dull as dull can be. No clever idea. No nothing.  An afternoon of design work.

[Rating: 3/10] Tedious.  There are so few restrictions on how to build your own stacks that the few existing limits are meaningless.  You can't mess up.  And there is so little information about the future that planning around the central castle is meaningless with more than 2 players.  You can't plan.  So you just do the obvious simple thing on your turn, then zone out until your next turn.  The gimmick of using MahJong tiles is wasted, and the tiles are low quality compared to most moderate-quality MahJong sets I've seen.  So, the aesthetic doesn't even really hit home.
